runbook:
Container anomaly response. A container on the triggering host exited, turned unhealthy or is restarting; the trigger gives its name and the event. Investigate read-only, then, only when it is likely to help, propose starting or restarting that one container for a person to approve. Never remove anything and never change how the container is defined.

Work on the triggering host and container only. Docker commands fail without access to the Docker socket; if they do, note it and report.

Investigate (read-only; anything else is refused):
1. State: `docker inspect --format '{{.Name}} restarts={{.RestartCount}} memory={{.HostConfig.Memory}} policy={{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name}} {{json .State}}' <name>`. Note Status, ExitCode, OOMKilled, Error, StartedAt, FinishedAt, the restart count, the restart policy, the memory limit in bytes (0 means none) and, if it has a health check, Health.Status, FailingStreak and the last Health.Log outputs. If the container no longer exists it was removed or recreated: run `docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}'`, report what runs now, and propose nothing.
2. Was it on purpose? Exit code 0, or 143 right after a stop, usually means a person or a deploy stopped it. If it is running again, healthy, and has not restarted since, report that it recovered, with severity info, and stop here.
3. Logs: `docker logs --tail 200 --timestamps <name>`. Find the last error before the exit or the failing health check. Long output is cut in the middle; the end is what matters.
4. Memory: while it runs, `docker stats --no-stream --format '{{.Name}} {{.CPUPerc}} {{.MemUsage}} {{.MemPerc}}' <name>`, against the limit from step 1. Kernel OOM kills: `journalctl -k --since -24h -g oom --no-pager -n 20` (if --grep is not supported, `journalctl -k --since -24h -p warning --no-pager -n 50`). Exit code 137 with OOMKilled true, or a kernel OOM line naming its process, means it ran out of memory.
5. Host, only when the logs point at it: `df -hP` (a full disk breaks databases and logging) and `free -m`.

Exit codes: 0 clean exit; 1 or 2 application error; 125 to 127 Docker could not run the command; 137 killed (out of memory or docker kill); 139 segmentation fault; 143 stopped with SIGTERM.

Decide whether starting or restarting can help. It can after a one-off crash, when a dependency it needed is back, or when the health log shows a stuck process. It cannot when it fails on every start (the restart count climbing, the same error each time), when it was killed for memory more than once (the limit or a leak needs a person), when the log shows a configuration, missing file, permission or full disk error, when it was stopped on purpose, or when its restart policy is already restarting it; then propose nothing and give the fix in the report.

When it can help, call propose_plan for the triggering host only, with exactly one of these:
- `docker start <name>`, for a container that exited and is not being restarted by its policy
- `docker restart <name>`, for one that runs but is unhealthy

Never propose: docker rm, rmi, kill, stop, update, rename, prune, volume, network, pull, run or exec; docker compose in any form; editing compose files, environment files or anything else; restarting the Docker daemon; acting on any other container.

Commands run without a terminal as the host's SSH user. If `id -u` is not 0 and Docker needs root on that host, prefix the command with `sudo -n`.

For the plan give: the command; the rationale with the state, exit code and log lines; the risk (open connections drop, and it may fail again the same way); the rollback (nothing to undo, the container's definition does not change); and read-only verify commands: `docker ps -a --filter name=<name> --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}'` and `docker inspect --format '{{.State.Status}} {{json .State.Health}}' <name>`.

Severity: critical if it is down or restarting in a loop, warning if it runs but is unhealthy, info if it recovered or was stopped on purpose.

In the report, give the container, its state and exit code, the cause with the log lines that show it, and the plan or why there is none.
